pl49854.description: An ancient "emporion" listed by Ptolemy on the east coast of India. He also remarks that it is the "aphoterion" (point of departure) for those sailing out to the Chryse Chersonnesos. BAtlas tentatively identifies it with modern Vilasa in the Ghodivari river delta in the east Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

pl50081.description: A modern village near the coast north from Chennai where an archaeologically attested seaport settlement flourished from the 3rd century BCE until the 15th century CE as attested by remnants of Chinese and Thai pottery -- as well as a Chinese coin. It is probably to be identified with Ptolemy's "Kottis".

pl50219.description: Dharanikota is a modern village adjoining Amaravathi on the southern bank of the Krishna river in Andhra Pradesh. Ancient habitation, attested by pottery, and a series of wharfs and water management structures in various materials including brick and stone, indicate that trade and settlement activity began at the site as early as the second century BCE. The site has been identified with Ptolemy's Pitoura, which he identifies as a "metropolis".

pl110853570.description: Ancient settlement and center of Buddhism near modern Banpur with remains from the 7th-12th centuries. Demolished in modern times.

q752091.dateNote: Built about 1250 under King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.

q664591.placeNote: Pinned at the centre of Andhra Pradesh. Wikidata records the country where this happened but not a place within it, so the marker shows the country, not the spot.

pl25660908.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl25660908.description: A modern city in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, Machilipatnam served as a major port on the Bay of Bengal, from the 16th through the 19th centuries. Some Roman coins and Mediterranean ceramics have been recovered in the area.

cur-fossil-kota.dateNote: In 1958 Indian Statistical Institute geologists found giant bones near Pochampally in the Pranhita–Godavari valley; digs in 1960–61 brought out the long-necked dinosaur Barapasaurus. The rock is about 190 million years old (Early Jurassic). Wikidata pins the formation at a rounded point.
cur-fossil-kota.summary: Where one of the first giant long-necked dinosaurs, Barapasaurus, was dug up in India.

pl454189058.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl454189058.description: Although the present city in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh seems to have been founded in the 11th or 12th century CE, archaeological evidence indicates the natural harbor at Visakhapatnam has served as a center of maritime trade from the 4th or 3rd century BCE onward.

pl119192778.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl119192778.description: An ancient settlement and modern town (also known as Mahabalipuram) located on the east coast of peninsular India. It is the site of a large complex of Hindu temples dating to the 7th/8th centuries CE that is registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The city is mentioned in Tamil literature beginning in the 8th century CE. The exact location of the city's harbor and its possible identification with non-Tamil sources (especially Roman ones) remain inconclusive.
